info.bio:
Sublime fue una banda de ska punk y reggae, originaria de Long Beach, California, formada en el año 1988.

La música de la banda ya de por si compleja, agregaba recursos del dub, funk y hip hop, dando pie para la creación de un extraño tipo de rock-steady mezclado con ska punk. 
Sublime estaba formada por tres integrantes Brad Nowell (voz y guitarra), Bud Gaugh (batería), y Eric Wilson (bajo). Lou Dog, el dálmata de Nowell, fué la mascota de la banda.

scenes.name: Hardcore en la era del punk-pop: emocore, ska-core y post-hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Mientras las revistas anuncian la «muerte del punk», el hardcore se convierte en un movimiento que no deja pueblo sin tocar y genera subgéneros. El «emocore» (Jawbreaker, Weezer, Sunny Day Real Estate, Promise Ring, At The Drive-In, Jimmy Eat World, Seaweed); el hardcore progresivo de Washington (Nation Of Ulysses, Make-Up, Shudder To Think, Jawbox, Edsel, Lungfish, Circus Lupus, Dismemberment Plan); el «ska-core» (Operation Ivy, Rancid, Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Sublime, No Doubt); el punk-pop que llega a las listas (Green Day, Offspring, Flop, Pennywise, Pegboy, Superchunk, Queers); el garage-punk californiano (Drive Like Jehu, Rocket From The Crypt, Blink 182, Zen Guerrilla); el jazzcore (Bazooka, Iceburn); la vieja escuela (D Generation, Supersuckers, Zeke, Dropkick Murphys, Silverfish, Turbonegro) y el post-hardcore de Unwound.
scenes.family: Punk, new wave, hardcore y noise

podcast.title: Sublime (Long Beach, 1988) – Co-Headlined First Vans Warped Tour 1995; Singer Brad Nowell Died of Heroin Overdose Two Months Before Major Label Album Came Out
podcast.body: Sublime came together in 1988 and had their own label (Skunk Records) by 1992. They became wildly popular by playing anywhere and everywhere, co-headlining the first Vans Warped Tour in 1995 and the first Sno-Core tour. After landing a major label deal, their first major label CD sold millions. Unfortunately, singer Brad Nowell died of a heroin overdose just two months before it came out. "Shortly after they also snagged a major label record deal and that first big label CD sold in the millions."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: A Not-So Brief History of Ska: Part 2

podcast.title: Singer Brad Nowell's Heroin Overdose (May 25, 1996)
podcast.body: Singer Brad Nowell died of a heroin overdose on May 25, 1996, at the Ocean View Motel in San Francisco, just as the band's self-titled album was completed and days after his marriage and months after his son's birth. Nowell, a long-term addict, accidentally injected a much stronger form of "Mexican brown tar heroin" than he was accustomed to. "One singer Brad Noel died of a heroin overdose on May 25, 1996 at the Ocean View Motel in San Francisco. He'd been an addict for some time, but he was used to Mexican brown tar heroin. What he injected that day was far stronger than he died. That was seven days after he got married and a couple of months since the birth of his son."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Great Lost Alt Rock Band" Status
podcast.body: Sublime is considered one of the "great lost alt rock bands of the decade," with speculation about what more they could have achieved had Brad Nowell lived, given the posthumous platinum and gold sales of albums featuring their recorded material. "That's why he called sublime one of the great lost bands of the 90s. Who knew what more they could have done had Brad lived?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Band Formation and Early Gigs
podcast.body: Sublime, featuring Bradley Nowell, Bud Gaugh, and Eric Wilson, began playing house parties in 1988, struggling to attract record labels due to their "punky Reggae band" style which was a hard sell at the time. "Sublime with Bud Gow and Eric Wilson started playing House Parties in 1988."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bradley Nowell's Cause of Death
podcast.body: Paramedics were called to the scene but it was too late; Bradley Nowell had died several hours earlier and was pronounced dead at the scene at the age of 28. "Paramedics were called, but it was too late. Bradley had died several hours earlier and was pronounced dead on the scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bradley Nowell's Death and Discovery
podcast.body: Bradley Nowell was found dead on the floor of his motel room the next morning by his bandmates, with his beloved Dalmatian, Lou Dog, whining on the bed beside him. Initially, they thought he was merely too drunk to get into bed, but then they observed a yellow film around his mouth. "Later that morning, they went to Bradley's room and found him on the floor with Lou Dog whining on the bed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bradley Nowell's Early Life and Musical Influence
podcast.body: Bradley Nowell experienced his parents' divorce, initially living with his mother before moving in with his father, who taught him guitar. During a sailing trip to the Virgin Islands with his father, Bradley was introduced to reggae, which he greatly loved. "Dad not only taught him how to play guitar, but the two of them also went sailing in the Virgin Islands where Bradley was introduced to Reggae."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bradley Nowell's Heroin Use Justification
podcast.body: Bradley Nowell developed a heavy heroin habit, believing that the drug helped him cope with and fulfill the demanding obligations of being a rock star. "At the same time though, Bradley fell into heroin use. He felt that the drug helped him live up to the obligations of being a rock star and he started using heavily."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bradley Nowell's Last Night and Morning
podcast.body: After a show in San Francisco on May 24, 1996, Bradley Nowell returned to the Ocean View Motel with his Dalmatian, Lou Dog. The next morning, he attempted to persuade his hungover bandmates to join him at the beach, but they chose to remain in bed. "After a show in San Francisco and made the 24th of 1996, everyone went back to the Ocean View Motel."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bradley Nowell's Son Takes Over Vocals
podcast.body: In 2024, Bradley Nowell's son, Jacob, assumed the role of lead vocalist for Sublime, continuing his father's legacy in the band. "In 2024, Bradley's son Jacob took over his lead vocalist."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bradley Nowell's Tour Schedule Leading to Death
podcast.body: In late May 1996, Sublime embarked on a tour that included dates in Northern California, planned subsequent swings through Europe, and a return for an American East Coast trek. "In late May 1996, Sublime was on a tour through Northern California, which was to be followed by a swing through Europe and then back for a trek up and down the American East Coast."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bud Gaugh Arrested Twice
podcast.body: The band's member, Bud, was arrested twice on the same day during a Warped Tour. "bud from sublime got arrested twice on the same day."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Drummer's Involvement in Eyes Adrift
podcast.body: The drummer from Sublime was a member of Chris Novoselic's post-Nirvana band, Eyes Adrift. "and the drummer from Sublime."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Career as a Garage Punk Band
podcast.body: Prior to 1995, Sublime was known as "just another garage punk band" originating from somewhere south of Los Angeles. They had released only two albums over seven years since their formation in 1988, having "been grinding it out" for a long time. "Before 1995, Sublime was really just another garage punk band from somewhere south of Los Angeles who had managed to release just two albums over seven years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Death as a Career Move ｜ From the Archives

podcast.title: Formation and Grassroots Following
podcast.body: Sublime was formed in 1988 and built a substantial grassroots following by performing countless gigs over the years. "Sublime was one of the great lost alt rock bands of the decade. They were formed in 1988 and muscled through countless gigs, building up a substantial grassroots following."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Heroin Decimation
podcast.body: Heroin tragically decimated and brought death to the band members of Sublime. "Heroin decimated and brought death to the New York dolls. The pretenders sublime, smashing pumpkins, allyson chains, skinny puppy holes, Scott Wylin, D.D. Ramone, Billy Eidle, a chunk of ever-clear, a vast swath of the Britpop scene of the 1990s, and pretty much everyone who's ever been in the Red Hot Chili Peppers past in present."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence from Fishbone
podcast.body: Sublime is among the bands that have cited Fishbone as an important influence on their music. "No doubt. Sublime."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Major Label Deal
podcast.body: After the success of their independent releases, Sublime secured a major record deal with MCA Records, indicating a turning point in their career. "Sublime got a few breaks which finally led to a major deal with MCA records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Major Label Deal and High Expectations
podcast.body: After releasing two independent albums, Sublime secured a major record deal with high expectations, believed to have the potential to achieve the same level of success as The Offspring or Green Day. "After two indie albums, they scored a major deal. And the thinking was that they could be as big as the offspring or Green Day."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Major Label Deal and High Expectations
podcast.body: After the success of their independent releases, Sublime secured a major record deal with MCA Records, indicating a turning point in their career. "Sublime got a few breaks which finally led to a major deal with MCA records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Massive Posthumous Sales
podcast.body: Sublime sold "a million times more records after Brad Noelle died," with a significant portion of the interest in the band stemming directly from his death. "In fact, a lot of the interest in Sublime was because he died."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Death as a Career Move ｜ From the Archives

podcast.title: Removed from Tour Over Dog
podcast.body: Sublime was asked to leave the Warped Tour because they insisted on bringing the band's dog, and the tour had a strict "no dog zone" policy. "sublime was asked to leave the tour because they insisted on bringing the band's dog and there was no dog zone."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sublime's Continuation After Nowell's Death
podcast.body: Despite the loss of their primary frontman, Sublime has continued to exist for many years, largely sustained by a substantial archive of recorded material and numerous live performances. "Despite the loss of their main guy, Sublime has continued all these years, thanks largely to a large backlog of recorded material and plenty of live gigs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Third Wave Ska Band
podcast.body: Sublime was identified as a band from the "third wave" of Ska, which arrived in the 1990s. This wave saw significant popularity with bands like No Doubt, The Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Reel Big Fish, Goldfinger, and Dance Hall Crashers. "Third wave Scott arrived in the 1990s, no doubt, muddy, muddy boss tones, sublime, real big fish, gold finger, dancehall crashes and so many more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

podcast.title: Timely Emergence in Southern California Punk Scene
podcast.body: The band found themselves "in the right place at the right time with the right songs" during the mid-1990s Southern California punk rock explosion. "They were one of those bands in the right place at the right time with the right songs when the whole Southern California punk rock explosion happened in the middle of 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Death as a Career Move ｜ From the Archives

podcast.title: Warped Tour Disruption
podcast.body: In 1996, the band's reputation was significantly boosted when they were ejected from the Warped Tour for being "too disruptive," signaling their readiness for major mainstream attention. "By 1996, their reputation was bolstered by being thrown off the warp tour for being too disrupted. I want to just think about that for a second. They were ready for prime time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: Bradley Nowell, identified as "Brad Noel" and the singer of Sublime, died in May 1995 from a drug overdose. "Brad Noel, singer, sublime, Drug Overdose, May 1995."

xref.title: Participant in First Warped Tour (1995)
xref.body: Deftones were among the approximately 20 up-and-coming alternative bands that performed on two stages during the inaugural Warped Tour in 1995. "For about 20 of them, sublime, deaf tones, L7 and a new group from Orange County called No Doubt."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Death by Heroin Overdose
xref.body: Died of a heroin overdose on May 25, 1996, after taking a "celebratory hit of heroin." This occurred just six weeks before Sublime's highly anticipated major label third album was scheduled to be released. "But before they could join the ranks of bands like Green Day and the offspring, the singer up and died of an overdose. His name was Bradley Noelle."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Eyes Adrift Formation and Disbandment
xref.body: Following Sweet 75, Chris formed Eyes Adrift with a member of the Meat Puppets (one of Nirvana's favorite bands) and the drummer from Sublime. This band also failed to attract an audience and was finished by 2003. "That was followed by a group called Eyes Adrift, with a guy from the Meet Puppets, one of Nirvana's favorite bands, and the drummer from Sublime."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Greater Posthumous Earnings
xref.body: Bradley Nowell ultimately "made more money dead than he ever did alive" due to the massive commercial success of Sublime's albums and releases following his death. "Sublime, featuring singer Brad Noelle, a guy who's made more money dead than he ever did alive."

xref.title: Studio Ownership and Academia
xref.body: Sylvia Massy owned her own studio for many years, which was a popular choice for bands like Sublime and Econoline Crush. Additionally, she has served as a visiting professor at Berklee College of Music and conducted workshops for the Abbey Road Institute, demonstrating her commitment to educating the next generation of audio professionals. "Sylvia owned her own studio for years, a place booked by Sublime, Econoline Crush and Dozens of Others."
